title: Formal Purpose: A Fin de Que and Con el Objeto de Que

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *para que* + subjunctive from B1 Unit 4. It gives the purpose of an action when the person in the second clause is not the person in the first: *Habla despacio para que te entiendan*. You also know *hablara* from B1 Unit 38: after a past verb the subjunctive moves to the imperfect (*pidió que hablara*). This lesson adds two more connectors with exactly the same grammar: *a fin de que* and *con el objeto de que*. Both mean "so that" or "in order that", and both sound more formal than *para que*, so you will see them in notices, announcements and writing. The rule stays the same: two different subjects, then the subjunctive. Use the present subjunctive after a present or future verb, and the imperfect subjunctive after a past verb.

sections.title: Three ways to say "so that"
rows: so that, in order that (more formal)
con el objeto de que + subjunctive
so that, in order that (formal, written)
Present or future verb: …, a fin de que vengan.
The subjunctive is in the present.
Past verb: …, a fin de que vinieran.
The subjunctive is in the imperfect.

items.spanish: La escuela organizó una reunión a fin de que los padres conocieran al director.
items.english: The school organised a meeting so that the parents could meet the head.

items.spanish: Cambiaremos el horario con el objeto de que todos puedan venir.
items.english: We will change the schedule so that everyone can come.

items.spanish: Te envío el plano a fin de que encuentres la casa sin problemas.
items.english: I am sending you the map so that you can find the house without problems.

items.spanish: Hablé con el jefe con el objeto de que nos diera más tiempo.
items.english: I spoke to the boss so that he would give us more time.

sections.content: These connectors need two different subjects. If the same person acts twice, use an infinitive instead (the next lesson). Never use the indicative or the future after them: say *a fin de que lleguen*, not *a fin de que llegan* or *llegarán*, and *a fin de que llegaran*, not *llegarían*, after a past verb. The meaning is the same as *para que*: choose the longer forms when you want a more formal tone.
